findings.message: `s` (store_sales) and `p` (pageviews) are joined with nothing relating them, so every row of one pairs with every row of the other: up to about 28 quadrillion pairs, fewer if filters or joins leave fewer rows. Bytes billed don't grow, but compute does, and counts or sums over the result are multiplied.
findings.fix: Add the condition that relates them. If every pair is intended, keep one side small, such as a single-row subquery or a short list of dates.

findings.message: `proj.web.pageviews` is clustered by `wiki`, then `title`. The query filters `title` but doesn't limit `wiki` to particular values, so BigQuery may skip far fewer blocks than it would with a `wiki` filter as well.
findings.fix: If the question is about particular `wiki` values, filter on them with `=` or `IN`.
